item.title: DarkMatterFM-Registry: A Machine-Readable Registry of Dark-Matter Models Extracted from the arXiv Literature
item.description: arXiv:2611.08583v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To use a dark-matter model one needs to know what defines it, which observables it affects, which codes and likelihoods evaluate it, and under what assumptions a published bound applies. That information is scattered across tens of thousands of papers. We present DarkMatterFM-Registry, a machine-readable registry of dark-matter models extracted from arXiv full texts by a staged large-language-model (LLM) pipeline: 6,145 structured model cards, validated against a seven-file JSON Schema suite, ranked by expected value for observational follow-up, and enriched for the top ~2,000 with observables, constraints, and theory-to-observable routes. Schema checks pass 97.8% of cards, and an LLM-judged accuracy study on a stratified card sample finds 81% of section verdicts correct, 18% partially correct, and none hallucinated. As a first application we turn the registry into a priority-weighted roadmap of 25 concrete projects the community could build. The roadmap is built by judging every computational step of every enriched model's theory-to-observable routes as available, partial, or missing, and aggregating the resulting typed gaps weighted by model priority. We find that what blocks the most high-priority models is not missing theory but missing shared infrastructure: model files for existing relic-abundance solvers, a general non-cold Boltzmann-code framework, reusable indirect-detection likelihoods, and a Lyman-$\alpha$ forest likelihood for non-cold dark matter (the largest gap for structure-formation probes). The model cards, schemas, roadmap, and ranking are released making the project reproducible and the cards available for the community.
item.dc:creator: Ioana A. Zelko, Jo Bovy, Nolan Koblischke

item.title: Primordial or Post-Inflationary: Distinguishing the Origin of Scale-Dependent Features in the CMB
item.description: arXiv:2611.08585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics beyond the Standard Model, whether of primordial or post-inflationary origin, can leave scale-dependent signals in the anisotropies of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). In this work, we study how distinguishable these broad classes of signals are and quantify their level of degeneracy. In this initial investigation, for primordial features, we limit ourselves to those of the ``sharp'' and ``resonant'' kinds; for post-inflationary features, we consider two qualitatively distinct models: exotic energy injection, which deposits energy into the primordial plasma and modifies the global thermodynamic history, and early dark energy (EDE), which affects the CMB through the background expansion and gravitational perturbations. By studying representative examples, we find that while primordial features can leave oscillatory signatures in the CMB power spectrum with essentially arbitrary frequency and running, the post-inflationary models considered here produce qualitatively different patterns that cannot generically reproduce the characteristic running of primordial feature oscillations. We verify these findings first with a principal component analysis, and show using only the most significant principal components that there are no significant degeneracies between the primordial and post-inflationary features considered here, and secondly with a full likelihood analysis, which shows that the resulting posteriors do not change significantly when considering individual classes of models or combinations of primordial/post-inflationary features. While the two post-inflationary models probe distinct physical mechanisms and both are implemented in a simplified, phenomenological fashion, the methods used in this work can be generalized to include more realistic signals or other classes of signals.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Braglia, Wenzer Qin, Xingang Chen, Tracy R. Slatyer

item.title: Anisotropic three-point statistics of the peculiar velocity and galaxy density fields: modelling in Fourier and configuration space
item.description: arXiv:2611.08589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By the equivalence principle, large-scale peculiar velocities provide a kinematical probe of the matter distribution independent of the biased galaxy distribution. Their three-point correlation with galaxies assesses the nonlinear coupling between cosmic flows and the surrounding density field. We develop a tree-level model of the anisotropic correlation between one line-of-sight peculiar velocity and two galaxy densities in redshift space, including quadratic and tidal galaxy bias. Starting from the corresponding velocity-divergence bispectrum, we derive predictions in both Fourier and configuration space through a spherical-harmonic expansion. We test the Fourier-space calculation against a closed-form expression and assess the numerical convergence of the configuration-space predictions. For a fiducial model, the signal is dominated by a dipolar dependence on triangle orientation relative to the line of sight, while subdominant multipoles distinguish the responses to growth and galaxy bias. In configuration space, the baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) feature depends on which triangle side crosses the acoustic scale and on the velocity projection. We also relate the model to the density-weighted statistic measured by peculiar-velocity catalogues and formulate estimators for its observable multipoles. This framework supports future measurements and covariance analyses needed to establish the additional cosmological information carried by velocity-density three-point correlations.
item.dc:creator: M. Guidi, A. Farina, A. Nusser, E. Branchini

item.title: VENUS: Strong Lens Mass Models and Einstein Radii of 60 Galaxy Clusters
item.description: arXiv:2611.08630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the strong lens mass modeling result of 60 galaxy clusters targeted by Vast Exploration for Nascent, Unexplored Sources (VENUS), the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) multi-epoch Treasury program. We obtain refined mass models for the 60 clusters with the glafic software by fitting positions of $\sim 4500$ multiple images, $\sim 1150$ of which are newly identified multiple images with help of multi-band JWST images. Each cluster contains typically $\sim 50$ multiple images, thanks to the selection of target clusters based on their high lensing strengths. We validate our models with the Jackknife method. The median Einstein radius is $\sim 30''$ and the distribution of the Einstein radii extends out to $\sim 60''$ for the source redshift of 9, which confirms that their lensing strengths are indeed among the highest known to date. For the source redshift of 9, we identify MACS J0717.5+3745, MACS J0600.1$-$2008, and PLCK G287.0+32.9 as clusters with the largest Einstein radii as well as the largest areas of the high-magnification ($|\mu|>10$) regions. We find that the observed Einstein radii of VENUS clusters are fully compatible with the standard cold dark matter model.

item.title: Short-term optical monitoring of quadruply imaged quasars
item.description: arXiv:2611.08633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present two case studies to demonstrate that short-term optical monitoring campaigns of quadruply imaged quasars (quads) reveal their astrophysical potential. Using the Liverpool Telescope and the third facility of the Two-meter Twin Telescope (TTT3), we monitored the quads QSO 2237+0305 and PS J0147+4630 in the gr bands between July 2025 and January 2026. For QSO 2237+0305, the resulting light curves revealed microlensing variability over a timescale of ~150 days. The g-band difference light curve between images A and B was then used to reliably constrain the half-light radius of the g-band source within the 3.5-16 lt-day range (1{\sigma} confidence level). For PS J0147+4630, we derived new constraints on the AB and AC time delays from the r-band light curves of the ABC images in an arc-like configuration, obtaining 2{\sigma} uncertainties of ~2 days. These constraints were used to shed light on the lensing mass distribution. Overall, our results validate the design of short-term optical monitoring campaigns of quads as valuable astrophysical tools in the era of large-scale surveys. The proof of concept relies on observations with ground-based 2mclass telescopes that lack sophisticated systems to correct for optical distortions caused by atmospheric turbulence, and we indicate the astro-photometric properties of the targets and the monitoring strategies needed to achieve success with these telescopes. Additionally, this work represents the first validation of the TTT3 facility for precision photometric monitoring of gravitationally lensed quasars.
item.dc:creator: L. J. Goicoechea, V. N. Shalyapin, A. Esteban-Guti\'errez, R. Gil-Merino, M. Serra-Ricart

item.title: Nonstandard Dark Matter at Nonlinear Scales
item.description: arXiv:2611.08636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how two extensions of the standard $\Lambda$CDM scenario affect the evolution of the matter density and velocity divergence fields, from the linear regime to deeply nonlinear scales, using $N$-body simulations. We consider two well-motivated scenarios in which the canonical properties of dark matter (DM) are modified. In the first scenario, DM interacts with dark energy (DM--DE interaction). In the second scenario, we allow the DM equation-of-state parameter to deviate from the canonical pressureless limit, $w_{\rm DM}=0$. For the coupled DM--DE scenario, we find significant and scale-dependent deviations from $\Lambda$CDM of order $50$--$100\%$ in the matter power spectrum, persisting throughout the nonlinear regime, with the velocity divergence spectra providing complementary and partially independent sensitivity. For the $w_{\rm DM} \neq 0$ scenario, we find systematic but remarkably small deviations confined within $5\%$ across all scales probed. Our results identify which scales carry the greatest discriminatory power between these nonstandard scenarios and $\Lambda$CDM. We show that testing these models with current and forthcoming LSS surveys, through the analysis of density and/or velocity fields, will require a deeper theoretical understanding and accurate nonlinear modelling before robust constraints can be derived from observational data.
item.dc:creator: Rafael C. Nunes

item.title: Modified Newtonian Dynamics and galaxy clusters
item.description: arXiv:2611.08702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: First proposed by Milgrom in 1983 as an alternative to the standard Cold Dark Matter (CDM) paradigm, Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) has gained renewed momentum in light of persistent non-detections of exotic dark matter particles and growing tensions facing CDM on galactic scales. While MOND perfectly reproduces galactic rotation curves, it encounters notable challenges in explaining the equilibrium of galaxy clusters. Although it reduces the overall dark matter budget in these massive systems, an unidentified mass component remains required. This paper investigates the hypothesis that this missing mass is baryonic: composed of non-radiating ordinary matter such as stellar remnants, gas too diffuse to initiate star formation, or compact, ultra-dense clouds of cold molecular gas with low volume filling factors. Using a sample of 106 clusters mapped in X-rays, emitted by the hot intra-cluster medium (ICM) composing most of the visible mass, we derive first the total mass within the Newtonian dynamics, assuming hydrostatic equilibrium and spherical symmetry. Then, with the modified Poisson equation, we reconstruct the spatial distribution of the invisible missing matter within the MOND framework. In the sample, the relaxed systems harboring cooling flows, known as cool-core clusters, have the highest peaks of dark missing mass. Its density profile reveals a pronounced central concentration bounded by a steep truncation immediately beyond a core radius of 20-30 kpc, confirming previous studies. MOND reduces the necessary dynamical mass by a factor of 4 to 10. The residual missing mass is proportional to the total gas mass, being roughly twice lower.
item.dc:creator: Francoise Combes (LUX, Obs-Paris)

item.title: Primordial non-Gaussianity as a large-scale cosmic-web bias
item.description: arXiv:2611.09362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Primordial non-Gaussianity is a unique probe of the physics of inflation, but its large-scale-structure signature is difficult to measure because it appears on the largest, most cosmic-variance-limited modes. The standard view of local-type primordial non-Gaussianity is isotropic: it induces a scale-dependent correction to tracer bias, $\Delta b(k)\propto f_{\rm NL}k^{-2}$, on large scales. Here we show that the same large-scale response can be reformulated as an anisotropic, nonlocal environmental-bias effect. Motivated by the spectral cosmic-web hierarchy of Kitaura and Sinigaglia, we define a Hessian field $\mathcal{H}_{ij}(\bf{x})\equiv\partial_i\partial_j\nabla^{-4}\delta(\bf{x})$, whose trace obeys $\mathrm{Tr}\mathcal{H}=\nabla^{-2}\delta$ and therefore carries the same $k^{-2}$ enhancement that appears in the Dalal et al. scale-dependent-bias term. Diagonalizing $\mathcal{H}_{ij}$ defines four large-scale web environments, analogous to knots, filaments, sheets, and voids, although operating on scales much larger than the conventional nonlinear cosmic web. We assign one weight to each environment and test the construction with the AbacusPNG suite of local-PNG $N$-body simulations, using $f_{\rm NL}=\{-100,-30,30,100\}$. We show that these four weights reproduce the large-scale $k^{-2}$ rise of the tracer bias. We further show that existing halo catalogs without PNG can be post-processed to imprint an effective $f_{\rm NL}$ signature. Beyond mock generation, the resulting cosmic-web response motivates an observational statistic based on changes in tracer occupation of large-scale environments relative to a matched Gaussian reference, complementary to the conventional low-$k$ power spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Kilian Peraza Vera, Francisco-Shu Kitaura, Francesco Sinigaglia

item.title: Through Ups and Downs: the Transient Lensing Behaviour of SIDM halos undergoing Core Collapse
item.description: arXiv:2611.09546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) haloes can become extremely dense following gravothermal core collapse, motivating their use as explanations for unusually concentrated gravitational lenses. Using an emulator calibrated on gravothermal fluid calculations, we investigate whether increasing central density necessarily strengthens lensing. We follow initially Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) haloes through core formation and collapse deep into the short-mean-free-path regime, and compute finite-source magnifications, critical curves, and source-plane lensing cross sections for isolated spherical haloes with elastic, velocity-independent self-interactions, including external shear in selected calculations. Lensing strength evolves non-monotonically: it initially decreases during core formation, rises during early collapse, and generally declines at later stages despite continued growth of the central density. This decline accompanies the emergence of a dense inner core whose mass and radius decrease within a more extended, lower-density core. Time-averaged enhancement relative to NFW haloes depends on the lensing statistic, halo concentration, and interaction cross section. Generalized NFW haloes with central cusps $\rho \propto r^{-\gamma}$ with $\gamma \geq 2$ always have larger lensing efficacies than core-collapsed SIDM haloes of equal mass and are therefore poor proxies, including in terms of the demographics (size and radial thickness) of arcs and Einstein rings. The core collapse stage at which SIDM haloes are optimal lenses coincides with the epoch at which the characteristic core surface density is close to critical, which typically occurs during the early stages of core collapse. These results demonstrate that central density alone is insufficient to characterize SIDM lensing and that its evolving mass distribution must be modelled explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Frank C. van den Bosch, Yarone M. Tokayer

item.title: Does DESI point towards transient cosmic acceleration?
item.description: arXiv:2611.09743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate an oscillatory equation of state for dark energy that oscillates around the mean value $-1$ and includes a source term proportional to the cube of the number of e-folds. Due to this source term, the oscillation amplitude shifts towards the $w_{\rm de}<-1$ regime at higher redshifts, whereas in the future, the source term drives the oscillation amplitude towards the $w_{\rm de}>-1$ regime. As the equation of state enters the $w_{\rm de}>-1$ regime in the future, the dark energy density dilutes, causing the Hubble parameter to decrease asymptotically towards zero, so that the present acceleration is transient: the Universe transitions to decelerated expansion and approaches a static state as $a\to\infty$, without ever contracting. We compare this equation of state with BellDE, CPL and flat $\Lambda$CDM. We confront the model with a combination of datasets, including Planck, DESI BAO and three different supernova compilations: Pantheon+, Union3 and DES-Dovekie. We compare the log-evidence of each model with that of $\Lambda$CDM. The dynamical dark energy models yield $H_0$ values in the range $66.0^{+0.80}_{-0.79}$--$67.84^{+0.69}_{-0.74}\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, with matter density values in the range $\Omega_{\rm m}=0.3067^{+0.0073}_{-0.0072}$--$0.3271^{+0.0083}_{-0.0080}$ across all the combinations. These values are consistent with those of the baseline model, apart from a mild upward shift in $\Omega_{\rm m}$ for the Union3 combination. Among all the models, BellDE yields comparatively stronger Bayesian evidence than the other models, with weak evidence for the Pantheon+ compilation and moderate evidence for the Union3 and DES-Dovekie compilations. The sourced oscillatory model yields inconclusive evidence for Pantheon + and Union3, while weak evidence for DES-Dovekie relative to $\Lambda$CDM.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Ahmad, Saddam Hussain, Ayodeji Ibitoye, Yi'an Zhao, Ming Zhang, Lang Cui

item.title: Odd Loops: What Structures Can Produce a Parity-Violating Inflationary Trispectrum?
item.description: arXiv:2611.09829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-Gaussian perturbations generated during inflation can often be described perturbatively via integrals of kernels acting on Gaussian fields. In this work, we investigate, in a model-independent manner, whether these kernels can produce parity-violating (PV) contributions to the trispectrum, and which Wick's theorem contraction configurations of the Gaussian fields lead to them. In detail, we evaluate all possible contraction configurations arising from the third- and second-order density perturbations. We find that, for the third-order perturbations, only one configuration can support PV contributions, as it retains three independent wave-vectors. In contrast, none of the four second-order perturbation contraction configurations can produce a PV contribution under statistical isotropy. These results offer a first step toward deriving kernels from inflationary models capable of generating a PV trispectrum. Such kernels could then be used to perform PV searches with current and upcoming galaxy redshift surveys such as DESI, Roman, SPHEREx, and Euclid, and photometric efforts such as LSST. Our results also offer a guide for exploration of PV with CMB data-sets such as Planck.
item.dc:creator: William Ortol\'a Leonard, Zachary Slepian

item.title: Lessons from double-plane lenses for galaxy profiles, the Hubble tension, and the mass-sheet degeneracy
item.description: arXiv:2611.09856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Double-plane lenses, like single-plane lenses, are subject to the mass-sheet degeneracy, a fundamental limit to our knowledge of the deflector mass profiles from lensing. However, with a prior on the relative expansion history, unlike in the single-plane case, this degeneracy can be constrained with the modelling of lens images, without the need for time delays, velocity dispersion measurements or a prior on the Hubble constant $H_0$. We show that double-plane lenses are sensitive to a specific combination of the mass-sheet components of the two lens planes. Using literature values of the cosmological scaling factor from the double-plane lenses J0946 and AGEL0353, a measurement from the point-source images of J1721 (the ``Einstein zig-zag'' lens), and a reference value of $\Omega_\mathrm{m}$, we show the constraints that can be placed on the mass-sheet component of each of these systems. We show that the additional information brought by images of a second source can improve measurements of $H_0$ from individual time-delay lenses by up to $\sim50\%$, depending on certain key assumptions. Using forecasted Euclid and LSST double-plane lens samples, we show that these samples will enable strong constraints on the population of mass sheets in lens galaxies. Such population constraints will have implications for a range of strong-lensing science applications, in particular in constraining $H_0$, dark energy, and the dark matter profiles of galaxies.
item.dc:creator: Daniel P. Johnson, Martin Millon, Pierre Fleury, Giacomo Queirolo, Tian Li, Wolfgang J. R. Enzi, Daniel J. Ballard, Duncan Bowden, Thomas E. Collett, Daniel Gilman

item.title: Unlocking Pandora's Secrets: Probing the Thermodynamics of Abell 2744
item.description: arXiv:2611.08847v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Abell 2744 (Pandora's Cluster) is a massive galaxy cluster undergoing multiple mergers, characterized by a highly disturbed X-ray morphology, elevated intracluster medium (ICM) temperatures, and several radio relics associated with merger driven shocks. We present NuSTAR observations of Abell 2744 aimed at mapping its thermodynamic structure and constraining the presence of inverse Compton (IC) scattering from relativistic electrons. We measure the temperature distribution across the cluster and identify a prominent shock front with a Mach number of $\mathcal{M} = 1.58^{+0.42}_{-0.30}$, aligning with the southeastern boundary of the radio halo. The global NuSTAR spectra are modeled with single- and two-temperature thermal components, as well as thermal plus power-law models to test for IC emission. The spectra are well described by purely thermal models with an average temperature of $kT \approx 11$ keV, and we find no significant evidence for non-thermal hard X-ray emission. We derive a 90\% confidence upper limit on the $20-80$ keV IC flux of $ F_{\rm nt} < 2.31 \times 10^{-12} erg~s^{-1}~cm^{-2}$. Combining this with 1.5 GHz diffuse radio measurements from the VLA, we estimate a lower limit on the average magnetic field strength of $B > 0.2 \ \rm{\mu G}$.
item.dc:creator: Randall Rojas Bolivar, Akos Bogdan, Daniel Wik, Gerrit Schellenberger

item.title: Violent relaxation redux
item.description: arXiv:2611.09531v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Collisionless self-gravitating systems, such as merging galaxies, have long seemed an exception to the statistical-mechanical principle that chaotic many-body systems relax to maximum-entropy states: Lynden-Bell's statistical mechanics of their "violent relaxation," constrained by exact conservation of phase-space volume -- equivalently, of infinitely many collisionless "Casimir" invariants -- has appeared not to be a good description. We propose that violent relaxation does give rise to Lynden-Bell's maximum-entropy equilibria, but that both are underpinned by gravitational turbulence, in which large-scale gravitational fluctuations drive chaotic phase-space mixing of the particles' distribution function. We derive the universal small-scale (sub-Jeans) spectra of this turbulence and show that it leads to phase-space-volume conservation being broken on a timescale only logarithmically longer, in the particle number N, than the dynamical (violent-relaxation) time. This timescale separation lets the system relax "adiabatically" through a sequence of Lynden-Bell equilibria, each corresponding to instantaneous values of the Casimirs. At long times, it approaches an equilibrium close to its "ground state": a distribution whose Casimirs have adjusted so that the system's energy is now its minimum possible energy. Thus, the system's universal tendency is toward a minimum-energy, maximum-entropy state. We corroborate this picture with 1D N-body simulations and hypothesize that it can explain the universal equilibria of galaxies and dark-matter halos.
item.dc:creator: Michael L. Nastac, Yonadav Barry Ginat, Robert J. Ewart, Michael Barnes, Alexander A. Schekochihin

item.title: Challenges for minimal warm inflation in the Standard Model and beyond
item.description: arXiv:2611.09893v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A minimal realisation of warm inflation, even within the Standard Model, assumes that the inflaton $\phi$ couples via the effective operator $\phi\, G\tilde G$. We show that the SM solutions are in tension with the plasma calculation (as each sphaleron transition releases an energy much larger than the temperature) and with the assumed effective operator description. Embedding $\phi$ as the Goldstone boson of a renormalizable Peccei-Quinn theory requires an anomaly coefficient $\gtrsim100$, implying a Landau pole for QCD. These tensions are relaxed for more strongly coupled dark gauge sectors.
item.dc:creator: Anish Ghoshal, Alessandro Strumia

item.title: Galaxy and Halo Root Systems: Fingerprints of Mass Assembly
item.description: arXiv:2503.21015v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We discuss what we call halo or galaxy root systems, collections of particle pathlines that show the infall of matter from the initial uniform distribution into a collapsed structure. The matter clumps as it falls in; projected through time, it produces filamentary density enhancements analogous to tree roots and branches, or branching river networks. This relates to the larger-scale cosmic web, but is defined locally about one of its nodes: a physical, geometric version of a merger tree. We find dark-matter-halo root systems on average to exhibit more roots and root branches for the largest cluster haloes than for small haloes, indicating their more complicated assembly, even in dark matter without gas physics. Also, we find that high spin manifests as curvier roots, and that many have mass contributions that start far away from central, compact protohalo cores. Root systems also show sensitivity to anisotropic infall, which we see some evidence for in a simulation with rather low box size.
item.dc:creator: Mark Neyrinck, Miguel Arag\'on-Calvo, Istv\'an Szapudi

item.title: How Significant are Cosmological Collider Signals in the Planck Data?
item.description: arXiv:2511.17500v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The search for primordial non-Gaussianities (PNG) is theoretically well motivated but remains observationally challenging. Tight constraints with low significance for the standard non-Gaussian shapes suggest that detection may lie beyond the reach of near-future experiments. However, tests of PNG are highly template-dependent. From a theory perspective, a whole new family of bispectrum shapes arise in the cosmological collider program, with distinct signatures of heavy particles during inflation. In this work, we provide a class of simplified collider templates for these particles that encompasses a broader range of masses, sound speeds, and interactions. We propose that, given the current state of observations, the most effective strategy to search for PNG signals is through orthogonalizing the collider templates, such that they are uncorrelated with the tightly constrained single field predictions. Our results show that removing the single-field contribution enhances the signal across all four templates studied. Using the {\it Modal} pipeline and \textit{Planck} CMB data, we perform a systematic parameter scan of the (\textit{orthogonalized}) collider templates with the most significant result reaching $2.4\sigma$ for spin-0, after taking into account the look-elsewhere effect; indicative results for spin-1 and spin-2 peak around 2$\sigma$. These results indicate that, with refined collider templates and improved data analysis strategies, there are credible prospects with forthcoming observations to detect PNG {\it and also} identify the presence of massive particles during inflation.
item.dc:creator: Petar Suman, Dong-Gang Wang, Wuhyun Sohn, James R. Fergusson, E. P. S. Shellard

item.title: An information-theoretic framework for quantifying coherence in the cosmic density field
item.description: arXiv:2601.02351v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce an information-theoretic framework for quantifying the coherence retained in the cosmic density field across cosmic time. Using mutual information between density fields at different redshifts in cosmological $N$-body simulations, and subtracting an appropriate reference baseline, we isolate the excess statistical dependence generated by gravitational evolution. Unlike conventional clustering statistics, this approach is sensitive to nonlinear and higher-order correlations and directly measures the shared information between different cosmic epochs. The shared mutual information exhibits a strong dependence on spatial scale, increasing as the density field is progressively coarse-grained, reaching a maximum, and declining at larger scales. Through a series of tests involving different simulation volumes, discretization schemes, alternative baseline constructions, and subvolume analyses, we show that the location of this maximum is governed primarily by finite-sampling effects in the mutual information estimator rather than by a fundamental physical coherence scale. The observed peak therefore provides an empirical indication of the range over which the present estimator yields robust measurements. We further demonstrate that the mutual information is sensitive to cosmic evolution and cosmological parameters. Our analysis shows that filamentary environments retain more statistically accessible shared information between cosmic epochs than sheets and clusters. We also note that the shared information between the initial and present-day density fields is found to be positive but extremely small, reflecting the progressive redistribution of information during nonlinear structure formation. Our results establish mutual information as a powerful new tool for quantifying coherence, memory, and information retention in the large-scale structure of the Universe.
item.dc:creator: Biswajit Pandey, Anindita Nandi

item.title: An efficient model of cosmology dependence in the covariance matrix of the matter power spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2601.13245v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Covariance matrices are essential for any cosmological likelihood analysis. They can be estimated from large suites of cosmological simulations, but this is computationally intensive, so various approximations are often adopted to simplify the analysis, such as treating covariance as being parameter independent to avoid having to compute matrices for every variation in physical parameters. In this paper, we develop a new approach to model the parameter dependence of the covariance matrix of the matter power spectrum. We do this by Taylor expanding the `true covariance matrix' around a fiducial point in parameter space projected onto a theoretically known precision matrix. In the limit that the known model approaches the true matrix then the Taylor expansion truncates at the first term; for more realistic models, additional terms are required. We use the publicly available Quijote suite of simulations, giving us both a fiducial model and variations in the six parameters $\{\Omega_{\rm m}, \Omega_{\rm b}, n_{\rm s},\sigma_{8}, h,w_{0}\}$. Using the linear power spectra from these simulations, we generate model covariance matrices with and without super-sample covariance. Using different approximations, we develop three versions of our interpolated covariance matrix and validate the formalism by recreating all of our input cosmologies using all three forms, both with and without super-sample covariance corrections, showing that the model provides good recreations of the original results, with the different approximations being optimal in different regimes. Our method enables rapid calculation of parameter dependent covariance matrices, and consequently precision matrices, for deployment in likelihood modelling codes.
item.dc:creator: Theodore Steele, Robert Smith

item.title: Universal Dark-matter Density Profiles of Cosmic Filaments
item.description: arXiv:2604.05033v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a comprehensive analysis of the radial dark-matter (DM) density profiles of cosmic filaments in the hydrodynamical simulation TNG50. The cosmic web is extracted from high-resolution density grids at redshifts $z =$ 0, 0.5, 1, 2 and 3 using the DisPerSE algorithm. We show that the filament spine locations returned directly by DisPerSE do not accurately reflect the true density ridges. To address this issue, we introduce a "shrinking-cylinder" re-centering algorithm, which significantly increases the inferred central densities and restores the inner power-law behavior of the profiles. When the radial coordinate is scaled by the virial radii of the terminal nodes, the filament density profiles exhibit a nearly universal form that depends only weakly on redshift, node mass, and filament length. This result suggests that cosmic filaments, much like dark-matter halos, obey a form of structural self-similarity once an appropriate characteristic scale is introduced. By repeating the measurement using only smoothly distributed, unbound DM particles, we find that the apparent central cusp of the full profile is primarily produced by low-mass halos embedded along the filament spines, while the smooth component develops a flat core within $R/R_{\rm vir}\lesssim0.1$. The redshift evolution of this smooth component further suggests a transition from predominantly smooth filamentary accretion at high redshift to increasingly clumpy accretion at late times. Finally, we show that the universal filament profile is accurately described by a generalized triple-power-law model.
item.dc:creator: Peng Xu, Fangzhou Jiang, Farhanul Hasan, Joanna Woo, Douglas Hellinger, Joel R. Primack, David C. Koo

item.title: TDCOSMO XXVI: Uniform lens modeling of eight doubly imaged quasars
item.description: arXiv:2604.24908v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the first uniform gravitational lens modeling analysis of eight doubly imaged quasars from multi-band observations with the Hubble Space Telescope. Previous time-delay cosmography analyses by the TDCOSMO Collaboration have primarily relied on quadruply imaged quasars, while doubly imaged systems, despite being more abundant, remain underutilized due to their fewer geometric constraints. Using an open-source $\texttt{Lenstronomy}$ framework, we reconstruct the lensing systems with a pipeline tailored for doubles. Comparing our results to the literature, the modeled Einstein radii agree at an average of 1.5$\sigma$, which is expected given data and modeling heterogeneity, while modeled image separations differ from Gaia DR2 measurements with an r.m.s of only 3.6 mas. We find a strong correlation between Fermat potential precision and the surface brightness of the spatially extended host arcs, establishing that arc surface brightness is the primary driver of mass model precision in doubly imaged systems. To further quantify the information contributed by the lensed arcs, we performed a conjugate point analysis that uses only the quasar image positions to constrain the lens mass profiles. The resulting posteriors are substantially broader than those from full image modeling, and a strong anti-correlation between mass parameter hypervolume and arc magnitude additionally confirms that arc brightness determines the degree to which the lens mass profile can be constrained in doubles. A hierarchical cosmographic analysis incorporating time-delay measurements and stellar kinematics to infer $\text{H}_0$ will be presented in a subsequent publication. The uniform pipeline and arc surface brightness trends established here will significantly accelerate the construction of time-delay cosmography samples from the large lens populations expected from LSST, Roman, and Euclid.

item.title: Cancellation of one-loop time dependence in superhorizon curvature perturbations from all scales
item.description: arXiv:2606.28247v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show the conservation of the superhorizon curvature perturbations at one-loop level in spatially-flat gauge, including contributions from loop wavenumbers on all scales in the decoupling limit, $\epsilon (\equiv -\dot H/H^2) \to 0$. In contrast to previous works, we do not assume a hierarchy $k \gg q$ between the wavenumber of the loop integral, $k$, and that of the power spectrum, $q$, and we explicitly include the regime $k \lesssim q$. Taking into account the nonlinear relation between the inflaton fluctuation and the curvature perturbation with the $\delta N$ formalism, we show that the apparent time dependence of the one-loop curvature power spectrum cancels once all contributions, including boundary terms, are combined consistently.
item.dc:creator: Keisuke Inomata

item.title: Effects of Solar Wind Plasma Noise on Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background Searches with a Space Based Interferometer Network
item.description: arXiv:2607.05368v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The LISA-Taiji dual detector network improves millihertz SGWB sensitivity through cross correlation measurements. Solar wind plasma, however, can generate plasma noise correlated between detectors and bias SGWB cross correlation estimates. We use high time resolution electron density data from Wind/SWE, estimate the solar wind electron density fluctuation spectrum with the Lomb-Scargle method, and propagate the resulting plasma noise to the TDI A/E channels of the LISA-Taiji network. By including finite arm propagation, Taylor frozen flow spatial correlations, and the network overlap reduction response, we compute the SGWB parameter bias induced by interdetector plasma noise. Although the single detector plasma residual is below the reference noise, the component correlated between detectors can enter the SGWB cross correlation estimator directly. Under dual detector scale coverage, the plasma induced parameter bias for a power law SGWB can reach $12.73\%$ of the corresponding Fisher parameter uncertainty. For M2/M3 cosmic string spectra, the bias in $\ln G\mu$ can reach $19.26\%$ of the corresponding Fisher parameter uncertainty for the network configurations, observing times, and frequency bands considered here. These results show that the impact of solar wind plasma noise cannot be assessed from the single detector residual noise level alone. In LISA-Taiji SGWB searches, the interdetector correlated component of this noise can directly affect parameter estimation.
item.dc:creator: Mengfei Sun, Borui Wang, Jie Wu, Jin Li, Shengyi Ye

item.title: Alcock-Paczynski Blinding Scheme for the Ly-$\alpha$ Forest Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2607.07875v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present and validate a blinding method for the Lyman-$\alpha$ (Ly$\alpha$) forest analysis based on a modification of the Alcock-Paczynski test. In order to hide the background expansion history, the method employs a geometrical shift of each quasar (QSO) forest in wavelength space, once the quasar continuum has been fitted and the fluctuation field is extracted. The redshift positions for the QSO sample are also changed in a consistent manner. We show that the method remains effective when applied to real data, where contamination from metals and Lyman-$\beta$ is intrinsically mixed with the Lyman-$\alpha$ forest. This limitation is primarily visible in the 1D correlation function, where other blinding strategies can mitigate the effect. To assess its effectiveness, the prescription is tested against a series of datasets of increasing complexity: from idealized low-noise mocks, to realistic DESI year one synthetic datasets, and finally to data from DESI first data release (DR1), using both the auto (Ly$\alpha\times$Ly$\alpha$) and cross (Ly$\alpha\times$ QSO) correlations. We find that the method robustly shifts the BAO peak position from the 3D correlation functions to the expected value for cosmology changes of around 5\% in the matter content, without altering the shape of the posteriors in the model parameters. In conclusion, this catalog-level blinding strategy is a viable method for cosmological inference with the Lyman-$\alpha$ forest, particularly if a cross-analysis with other tracers using the same blinding strategy is pursued.

item.title: Primordial tensor mode from the neutrino sector
item.description: arXiv:2607.15335v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that a regular solution for primordial tensor fluctuations can arise from the higher-order multipoles of the collisionless neutrino distribution after neutrino decoupling. Focusing on the leading case with the neutrino octupole mode (tensor-octupole mode), we derive the initial conditions for the Einstein-Boltzmann system and calculate angular power spectra for the cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropies. Compared with the standard gravitational-wave mode, the tensor-octupole mode has a weaker large-scale metric response. It therefore gives a suppressed reionization bump and a different oscillation phase in the tensor CMB power spectra, providing a way to separate it from the standard tensor mode.
item.dc:creator: Shohei Saga, Shuichiro Yokoyama

item.title: A low value of $H_0$ in tension with the distance ladder from Megamasers using peculiar velocity reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2608.06247v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Megamaser distances can be measured without using the traditional distance ladder. As such, they provide an independent probe of the local expansion rate, quantified by the Hubble constant $H_0$. We re-analyze megamaser distance and redshift data to obtain a new, more accurate, estimate of $H_0$. The main improvement in our analysis is the use of a new velocity field reconstruction to correct redshifts for peculiar velocities. This reconstruction utilizes constrained cosmological simulations in addition to redshift survey data to more accurately capture both coherent flows as well as nonGaussian individual galaxy motions. We argue that previous estimates of $H_0$ from megamaser data were susceptible to bias due to peculiar velocities. By correcting for peculiar motions using this new reconstruction we obtain a value of $H_0$ that is more consistent with the value from the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) than that of the distance ladder, although consistent with both, whereas previous results showed consistency with the distance ladder and tension with the CMB at greater than $2\sigma$. Our results suggest that the Hubble tension may be due to some heretofore undetermined systematic in the distance ladder rather than new physics.
item.dc:creator: Richard Watkins, Hume A. Feldman

item.title: Average soft X-ray surface brightness profile of massive galaxy clusters in Magneticum simulations
item.description: arXiv:2608.06619v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The self-similar growth of massive galaxy clusters suggests that radial profiles of their key thermodynamic properties should have identical shapes after proper mass- and redshift-dependent re-scaling. This property, tested within the virial radius on samples of well-studied individual objects, together with clear and robust observational characteristics such as sensitivity and background accounting, enables the possibility of stacking observations that can be confronted with identically-derived population-averaged predictions from theory or numerical simulations at large radii. Such a comparison not only eliminates effects of inevitable stochasticity in properties of individual objects, but also allows one to reach higher sensitivity for the faintest regions on the outskirts of the clusters. In this study, we conduct a one-to-one comparison of the observed and simulated average soft X-ray surface brightness profiles of several dozen massive galaxy clusters at low redshift. We find a very good out-of-the-box agreement between the 0.3 - 2.3 keV surface brightness profile of stacked galaxy clusters recently measured by SRG/eROSITA and the corresponding predictions from the Magneticum cosmological hydrodynamical simulations, which are known to reproduce other scaling relations observed for massive galaxy clusters. A significant difference between the observed and simulated profiles is present in the very central region, where effective implementation of the AGN feedback likely results in excessive gas redistribution within the core. The simulations predict a very noisy surface brightness profile beyond several times the virial radius of the cluster, with the mean signal being orders of magnitude lower than the local radially-flat but strongly fluctuating emission background, meaning that a proper detection of this component would be very challenging even with larger samples in the future.
item.dc:creator: A. Kruglov, N. Lyskova, I. Khabibullin, V. Biffi, K. Dolag

item.title: PIFFLE: Characterizing Foreground Dispersion Measure Contributions Across 4 Decades in Halo Mass in the FRB20230907D Field
item.description: arXiv:2608.28374v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterize the foreground environment of FRB20230907D, localized to a galaxy at $z=0.464$, which has an observed dispersion measure of ${\rm DM}_{\rm obs}=1031~{\rm pc~cm^{-3}}$. At its redshift, FRB20230907D lies above the Macquart relation, the expected relation between cosmological dispersion measure and the source redshift, indicating a substantial excess DM along this line of sight. We use Subaru/PFS and SDSS spectroscopy, published group catalogs, Rubin/LSST imaging, and eROSITA X-ray data to characterize the foreground structures that may account for this excess. A friends-of-friends search identifies a massive foreground system at $z\simeq0.09$ with $M_{\rm vir}\simeq7.7\times10^{14}~M_\odot$, while low redshift catalogs reveal an additional group at $z\simeq0.02565$. Assuming that the halo gas follows a modified-NFW halo density profile, we estimate observer frame contributions of $205^{+30}_{-25}~{\rm pc~cm^{-3}}$ and $80^{+60}_{-40}~{\rm pc~cm^{-3}}$ from these systems, respectively. After accounting for the remaining foreground and host contributions, we are able to make the first-ever constraints on the dispersion measure of a closely-intersected $M_*\approx 10^8\,M_\odot$ dwarf galaxy: ${\rm DM}_{\rm UGC7596}=58^{+53}_{-40}~{\rm pc~cm^{-3}}$ at $b_\perp \approx 0.03\,R_{\rm vir}$, which is consistent with hydrodynamical predictions for low mass halos. This highlights the enhancement of dense foreground spectroscopy and multi-wavelength data toward the interpretation of FRB dispersion measures.
item.dc:creator: Qi Guo, Khee-Gan Lee, Sunil Simha, Chenze Dong, Ilya S. Khrykin, Nicolas Tejos, J. Xavier Prochaska, Kevin McCarthy, John D. Silverman, Ines Pastor-Marazuela, Ben Stappers, K. M. Rajwade, Manisha Caleb, Bonny Y. Wang, Leander Thiele, Zhao Joseph Zhang, Kentaro Nagamine

item.title: Mitigating prior-volume effects in galaxy clustering by adopting Mpc over Mpc/h units
item.description: arXiv:2610.08751v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate prior-volume effects in Bayesian analyses of galaxy clustering based on state-of-the-art models, such as the EFT and the VDG$_\infty$ model. We show that these effects are largely driven by imposing priors on the model parameters defined in ${\rm Mpc}/h$ units, thereby introducing a spurious correlation with the Hubble parameter $h$, and that they can be strongly mitigated by adopting a more physically motivated formulation in ${\rm Mpc}$ units. We test this approach using a set of synthetic data vectors designed to reproduce the clustering signal expected in a Stage-IV survey across a range of cosmological models, including $\Lambda$CDM, $K$CDM, $w$CDM, and $w_0w_a$CDM. We find that the resulting constraints are largely free from shifts induced during the marginalisation process, even in the challenging $w_0w_a$CDM runs, reducing discrepancies with the fiducial values from several standard deviations to well within $1\sigma$. The performance of this approach is comparable to that of alternative mitigation strategies, such as the adoption of invariant priors or the reparametrisation of nuisance parameters in terms of growth and geometrical amplitudes. For the latter, we find that using $\sigma_{12}$ in place of the commonly adopted $\sigma_8$ to describe the amplitude of density fluctuations improves the performance of the reparametrisation technique, even at high redshifts, where constraints on the dark-energy equation of state are weaker. We further show that these conclusions hold with the inclusion of additional BAO constraints, and for data sets with reduced statistical power. These results add to the benefits of working with ${\rm Mpc}$ units, avoiding an explicit dependence on $h$, with direct relevance for the analyses of Stage-IV galaxy surveys.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Pezzotta, Alejandro P\'erez-Fern\'andez, Giosu\`e Gambardella, Ariel G. S\'anchez, Alexander Eggemeier, Martin Crocce, Benjamin Camacho-Quevedo

item.title: Gravitational waves from strong first-order phase transitions in an expanding Universe
item.description: arXiv:2610.14806v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the gravitational waves generated by first-order phase transitions (PTs) in an expanding Universe. Using a scalar field-fluid coupled model, we perform three-dimensional lattice numerical simulations of slow first-order PTs with strong strength. We observe that the contribution from sound waves to the gravitational wave (GW) signal significantly dominates over that from bubble collisions. The sound wave spectra exhibit two peaks located at the mean bubble separation and the sound-shell width. Rotational modes are generated in the fluid during the bubble collisions, and their magnitude grows with the PT strength ($\alpha$). The effective lifetime of the sound-wave source increases for slower PTs, decreasing for faster PT with larger $\beta/H$ and rising with smaller $\alpha$. While the simulated amplitude of normalized gravitational waves is of order $\mathcal{O}(10^{-2})$, in alignment with Minkowski-spacetime results, the resulting GW spectra differ markedly from those scenarios.
item.dc:creator: Jintao Zou, Zizhuo Zhao, Yongtao Jia, Ligong Bian

item.title: FOMO-Z. Optimal galaxy classification, photometric redshifts, and reconstruction of population distributions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40875v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present FOMO-Z (Flexible Optimizer of Multi-dimensional Operators and photo-$z$s), a set of statistical methods implemented in Python for galaxy classification and probabilistic inference from photometry. The methods use a reference sample with known galaxy properties. They rely on explicit, physically interpretable criteria and make no assumptions about the functional form of the color distributions. Binary selections are calibrated using either linear color conditions, particularly suited to background galaxy selection, or flexible color--color grids, seeking to maximize completeness given a threshold on purity. For probabilistic inference, the code identifies reference objects with compatible colors within photometric uncertainties to estimate each test galaxy's probability of satisfying user-defined criteria, as well as probability density functions of continuous properties such as redshift. The code also reconstructs property distributions of selected galaxy populations using photometrically similar galaxies in the reference sample. This framework supports prior weights and reference redshift probability distributions. A built-in feature-selection method identifying informative colors is also introduced. We demonstrate applications to background galaxy selection, galaxy population classification, tomographic redshift calibration, and photometric redshift estimation. The code achieves results consistent with those obtained through machine-learning approaches, such as self-organizing maps, while remaining computationally efficient, making it suitable for large photometric surveys and future Stage IV cosmological analyses. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/GiorgioLesci/FOMO-Z.
item.dc:creator: G. F. Lesci

item.title: Targeting the future of spectroscopic galaxy surveys -- A cosmological study case with the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope
item.description: arXiv:2611.02828v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The next generation of Stage-V spectroscopic surveys are designed to measure hundreds of millions of galaxy and quasar spectra, extending precision large-scale-structure cosmology to redshifts and volumes well beyond the reach of current Stage-IV facilities. Realising this potential requires revisiting the target selection strategies and designing them explicitly around the depth, multiplexing, and survey time of the new instruments, rather than a direct extrapolation of existing recipes. This work develops and characterises new strategies for the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST), a proposed 12-metre, highly multiplexed facility expected to operate in the 2040s. Using deep multi-band photometry, including COSMOS-field data from CLAUDS and HSC, we revisit low-redshift $z \lesssim 1.6$ tracer selection of SDSS, BOSS/eBOSS, DESI and 4MOST-CRS -- Bright Galaxies, Luminous Red Galaxies, Emission Line Galaxies and quasars -- to photometric depth achievable in the WST era, and introduce a purely magnitude-limited sample (MagMax) exploiting three-dimensional color-color star-galaxy separation, and a set of Lyman-Break Galaxy dropout samples extending target selection to $z \gtrsim 2$. Using Fisher-matrix forecasts, we showcase the constraining power of a WST-like cosmological survey on BAO distance parameters $\alpha_\parallel$ and $\alpha_\perp$, the growth rate $f$, the evolving dark energy equation $w_0w_a$, the local-type primordial non-Gaussianity $f_{\rm NL}^{\rm loc}$, and the sum of the neutrino mass $\Sigma m_\nu$. The main outcome of this work is an optimisation framework that directly links instrumental capabilities and observing time to cosmological constraining power, providing a science-driven template applicable to the design of future generations of Stage-V spectroscopic surveys.
item.dc:creator: Constantin Payerne (WST collaboration), Antoine Rocher (WST collaboration), Aur\'elien Verdier (WST collaboration), William d'Assignies (WST collaboration), Behnood Bandi (WST collaboration), Sofia Contarini (WST collaboration), Matteo Ferro (WST collaboration), Jean-Paul Kneib (WST collaboration), Vincenzo Mainieri (WST collaboration), Michele Moresco (WST collaboration), Marco Palla (WST collaboration), Maxime Rombach (WST collaboration), Christophe Y\`eche (WST collaboration), Furkan Akbaba (WST collaboration), H\'el\`ene Courtois (WST collaboration), Darko Donevski (WST collaboration), Massimo Guidi (WST collaboration), Valentin Ivanov (WST collaboration), Konstantinos Migkas (WST collaboration), Ivan Minchev (WST collaboration), Ignacio del Moral-Castro (WST collaboration), Olcay Plevne (WST collaboration), Mojtaba Raouf (WST collaboration), Laurence Tresse (WST collaboration)

item.title: Asymmetric Dark Matter from Low-Scale Spontaneous Leptogenesis
item.description: arXiv:2601.01849v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate a novel type of asymmetric dark matter (ADM) model in which the dark matter asymmetry and the baryon asymmetry in our universe (BAU) are produced simultaneously via low-scale spontaneous leptogenesis, where the mass scale of right-handed neutrino is much lower than the Davidson-Ibarra bound $M_1 \ll 10^{9}~\rm{GeV}$. In our scenario, both asymmetries are predominantly sourced by a dynamical $CP$ phase, namely the majoron. Its kinetic misalignment provides a sufficiently large, time-dependent effective $CP$ phase, allowing efficient asymmetry production even for low-scale right-handed neutrinos. In our framework, the sources of $CP$ violation responsible for the BAU and ADM are correlated with each other, leading to a predictive relation for the dark matter mass. In particular, when the dark matter asymmetry reaches its equilibrium value before freeze-out, the dark matter mass is typically predicted to lie in the range $\mathcal{O}(0.1)~\mathrm{GeV} \lesssim m_{\chi} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(100)~\mathrm{GeV}$, which lies within the sensitivity of direct detection experiments. On the other hand, if the dark matter asymmetry does not reach its equilibrium value due to weak coupling, the allowed mass range extends over a broader interval, $\mathcal{O}(0.1)~\mathrm{GeV} \lesssim m_{\chi} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10)~\rm{TeV}$.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Takahashi, Juntaro Wada

item.title: The Baryon Budget of Galaxies across the First Billion Years
item.description: arXiv:2603.00230v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a complete census of the baryons in early galaxies to investigate the phases in which gas and stars reside, their corresponding budgets, depletion times, and stellar return fraction as a function of redshift and stellar age. We use the ColdSIM hydrodynamical time-dependent non-equilibrium chemistry simulations and perform a detailed analysis of the cold, warm, hot, and stellar phases for both bound structures (galaxies/CGM) and the diffuse IGM. We investigate in depth the cold HI and H2 components, explicitly computed in our simulations, and their relations with host mass, SFR, metallicity and depletion times. We also provide observational insights and discuss the implications for stellar mass functions, PopIII star formation and changes in the IMF. We find that cosmic gas prior to reionisation is mostly cold, while at later epochs the warm phase becomes dominant due to enhanced star formation activity and increasing UV reionising radiation. Stellar return fractions at these times are ~0.15-0.20, a factor of two lower than the values usually adopted. Cold, warm, and hot gas masses as well as HI and H2 components show increasing trends with mass and SFR, while depletion times decrease down to 0.01-0.1 Gyr with a weak metallicity dependence. The resulting star formation efficiency remains at the level of a few per cent and gas-to-star fractions decline with mass, influenced by local feedback and environment. Our findings are consistent with ALMA, VLA and IRAM surveys at later epochs, including ALFALFA, xCOLDGASS, GASS, xGASS, EDGE-CALIFA, PHIBBS, and ASPECS. Gas phases are quantitatively related to the underlying stellar populations and can be used to infer unknown quantities. In the appendix we provide fit functions describing the trends of the stellar return fraction, the main sequence, phase mass relations, gas-to-star fractions and depletion times.
item.dc:creator: Umberto Maio, C\'eline P\'eroux

item.title: Graviton Floor
item.description: arXiv:2606.19757v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It has been observed that the Universe is permeated by the cosmic photon background, ranging from radio waves to gamma rays. We investigate the conversion of the photon background into gravitons in the presence of background magnetic fields in the Milky Way Galaxy and in blazar jets. We find that the resulting graviton background is dominated by the contribution generated in blazar jets. Importantly, this graviton background constitutes a graviton floor for high-frequency gravitational wave detectors searching for new physics, analogous to the neutrino floor.
item.dc:creator: Himeka Matsuo, Asuka Ito, Kazunori Kohri, Teruaki Suyama, Ryutaro Tomomatsu
